findings.title: The finale's reveal is fully legible in scene 3's frame, three scenes before it is narrated as a reveal
findings.evidence: scene_3.png: the bottom ~40% of the frame is the card 'Children treated — the figure, and the measurement' with all three of the finale's numbers rendered at full size — 58,251 Courses delivered, 88 / 108 Recorded recoveries in the observed sample, and 81.5% Observed recovery rate in the highlighted (blue-bordered) tile, each with its method paragraph beneath. Scene 6's narration then introduces exactly these as new: 'Beside it now sits a different figure — children with a recorded recovery ... The two do not agree.' The prior run's acceptance test (these figures appear in no frame before scene 6) still fails; the scene-3 recipe note claims a fix, but scrolling to that card's own .method-note lands the viewport with the payoff card immediately below it and fully in shot.
findings.why_it_costs: The one thing the whole narrative is built to deliver — that the number everyone quotes disagrees with the measured one — is spent in a scene about unit conversion. By scene 6 the only genuinely new material is the drill modal, so the finale reads as a detail on something already shown rather than the arrival.
fix_options: Re-point scene 3's camera so the frame ends at the 'What a dollar bought' method paragraph — scroll to that card and offset upward, or scroll to the ladder row and hold, so the following card is below the fold.
If the viewport cannot exclude it, move the two-figures card lower in the funder page (below the fold from the ladder) so scene 3 physically cannot contain it.
Failing both, cut the reveal from scene 6's narration and re-cut the finale to be about the drill alone — but this is the weakest option: the disagreement is the story.
findings.acceptance_test: In every frame before scene 6, none of '58,251', '88 / 108', '81.5%' or the card heading 'Children treated — the figure, and the measurement' is visible.

findings.title: Scenes 1 and 2 are one picture 179 px apart; the artifact scene 1's claim rests on is never framed
findings.evidence: Aligning scene_1.png and scene_2.png at a 179 px vertical offset leaves a mean absolute pixel difference of 2.3/255 — they are the same capture, scrolled. The Sankey is whole in scene 1 (y≈387–670) and whole again in scene 2 (y≈209–490); scene 2's only new content is the conservation caption and the top header row of the 'Stage by stage, per contract' table. Meanwhile scene 1's concept_claim ('three separate figures per contract ... never summed') has no on-screen referent: the per-contract obligated → disbursed → delivered bars are below the fold in scene 1, are only a header row in scene 2, and appear solely as a cropped sliver in the top ~90 px of scene 3 (the OES-C-2026-SD1 row), a scene about something else.
findings.why_it_costs: The rubric caps escalation at 2 for two scenes on one surface separated by a scroll. It also wastes the opening: the viewer hears the demo's founding distinction (committed vs paid vs delivered) over a frame that shows a funding diagram belonging to the next beat.
fix_options: Frame scene 1 on the key row PLUS the per-contract table — scroll to css:.contract-table (or equivalent) so the three-stage bars are the dominant object, and let the key figures ride at the top edge.

Alternatively hold scene 1 on the key row alone at scroll top and give scene 2 the Sankey, which is what the recipe intends but not what the frames show — requires the key row and the Sankey not to co-occupy one viewport.
findings.acceptance_test: Scene 1 and scene 2 differ by more than a pure vertical translation (no offset yields mean abs diff < 10/255), AND at least two contracts' three-stage bars are visible in scene 1's frame.

findings.title: The return from Hauwa to Dale at scene 6 is not motivated in the narration
findings.evidence: Scene 4's switch INTO Hauwa is explicitly set up ('Hauwa coordinates Nigeria's response and gets a version of this scoped to Nigeria'), and scene_4.png / scene_5.png carry the 'Government observer · Hauwa Ibrahim' chip. Scene 6's narration opens 'Here is the number every report leads with' and only names Dale mid-paragraph ('Dale can follow a single delivered batch'); nothing says we have left Nigeria's districts or why. The spec's `show` field says 'Back on the funder view' — the spoken track does not.
findings.why_it_costs: The viewer is moved from a Nigerian coverage table to a global funder page mid-sentence. It is the only place in the run where whose screen this is has to be inferred from the header chip.
fix_options: Open scene 6's narration with the handback — e.g. 'Hauwa's coverage number is only as good as the delivery figure behind it, so back on Dale's view, here is the number every report leads with …'
Or make the return load-bearing: state that the uncovered-children figure Hauwa just read is computed from the same courses figure Dale is about to have challenged.
findings.acceptance_test: Scene 6's first sentence names the persona change and gives a reason for it.

findings.title: Three different 'courses' magnitudes cross the sequence with no narrated bridge
findings.evidence: scene_1.png key row: '33,000 · Courses delivered under contract'. scene_3.png ladder: '12,000 · children given a full course, paid for and confirmed'. scene_3.png / scene_6.png card: '58,251 · Courses delivered'. Each carries its own method on screen and is individually defensible, but the narration for scenes 1, 3 and 6 never acknowledges that the headline count falls from 33,000 to 12,000 and then rises to 58,251 across three consecutive beats.
findings.why_it_costs: The run's whole thesis is that a figure is trustworthy when its method is on screen. A viewer tracking the number across the sequence sees it move twice without being told it moved — which is the exact suspicion the demo exists to disarm. Note this is a sequence-level gap only: no single frame contradicts itself, so the per-scene judges cannot see it.
fix_options: Add one clause to scene 3's narration acknowledging the narrowing ('of the 33,000 under contract, 12,000 are paid-for and confirmed — that is what this ladder prices').
Or add one clause to scene 6 naming the widening explicitly before the comparison ('58,251 — wider than the contract ladder, because it counts every carton that crossed a district from any source').
findings.acceptance_test: At least one narration beat explicitly relates the ladder figure to the key-row figure, and one relates the 58,251 card to the ladder figure.

The map fallback is out of frame entirely, and the page text confirms it is now a two-line 'Map not drawn' note rather than a panel. The 'Government observer · Hauwa Ibrahim' chip is in shot, so the scoping claim has a visible owner.

The scope inversion is gone. Hauwa's Nigeria page now reads 25,863 courses delivered against Dale's 33,000 under contract / 58,251 all-sources — narrowing scope now lowers the number. Carton-derived tiles are labelled 'Courses delivered' / 'Cartons delivered into districts'; the only surviving 'children' wording sits on measured-outcome fields (children needing treatment, children still uncovered, recorded recoveries), which is correct.
